notices.agency_name: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
notices.description: The Statara consumer dataset provides information on over 5.5 million adult New Yorkers. This serves as a single data source that provides far broader coverage than PEU can get from various partner agency sources. Having this broad coverage is critical during emergencies and also helps PEU reach New Yorkers who have fewer existing touchpoints with the City. Without the consumer file in question, PEUs efforts to reach out to underserved New Yorkers, especially during and after emergencies, will be greatly impaired. This procurement is therefore necessary for continuation of critical agency functions, a Mayoral Priority, and directly related to public health and safety. An annual license for a consumer detail analytics file install, including updated and refreshed cell phone contact data available for NYC to house in your internal analytics database. This will include NYC residents that may be overlooked on traditional publicly available and privately sourced data sets. An annual license for consumer details to house inside of your separately licensed CRM database.
notices.plain: The Human Resources Administration awarded Compulink Technologies Inc a $99,495 contract, without open competition as a minority- or women-owned small business, to subscribe to three licenses for the Statara consumer dataset, which the notice says helps the city reach underserved New Yorkers during emergencies.

The NYC Department of Small Business Services is entering into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension Contract with New York Committee for Occupational Safety and Health Inc to provide site safety training in the borough of Manhattan. Local Law 196 (2017) establishes Site Safety Training requirements for workers at most construction sites in the City of New York. Local Law 196 also requires that an agency designated by the Mayor will develop a program to provide equal access to the training required by Section 3321 of the New York City Building Code. The New York City Department of Small Business Services (SBS) has been designated to provide such a training program and to ensure that these essential safety standards are in place to protect the lives of construction workers and the public consistent with the requirements outlined in the local law. The contract term will be from 7/1/2026 to 6/30/2027, in the amount of $344,203.00

The services required under this contract are required to maintain the level of services required to be provided to construction site safety day laborer individuals until a new solicitation can be released and a new contract awarded.

Members of the public may register for a livestream of the hearing on Webex at:  

https://nycbp.webex.com/weblink/register/rb692af25c463a951dcfe91294ef31e87 

Testimony at the hearing is limited to 2 minutes, unless extended by the Chair. Testimony on these items will be accepted in-person, virtually, and in writing via email. To submit testimony virtually, register at the link above and select which agenda item you would like to submit comment for. While pre-registration is preferred, it is not required to speak; during the hearing there will be a call for testimony from those who have not signed up in advance.
